Print and read a settings assessment

Source: R/settings_assessment.R
print.terradish_setting_assessment.Rd

Compact display for the object returned by terradish_assess_settings: the graph profile, the recommended computational settings and why each was chosen, the probe timings behind them, and any warnings the assessment raised.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'terradish_setting_assessment'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class terradish_setting_assessment, from terradish_assess_settings.

digits

Number of significant digits used when formatting the probe timing tables.

...

Ignored, present for compatibility with the print generic.

Value

x, invisibly. Called for the printed output. The machine readable pieces are x$profile, x$recommended, x$reasons, x$benchmarks, x$comparison, and x$notes.

Details

How to read the output. It comes in four parts.

Graph reports the size of the problem: vertices (active raster cells), edges, focal sites, and conductance parameters. This is the number that decides whether any of the rest matters. Below roughly 50,000 vertices the defaults are almost always fine; above a few hundred thousand, solver choice dominates the runtime.

Recommended settings lists the optimizer, line search, solver, and approximation the probes favored, each followed by a parenthesized reason. Pass them straight through with fit <- terradish(..., optimizer = rec$optimizer, control = rec$control, solver = rec$solver), where rec <- assessment$recommended. These choices change only the computational path, never the estimates.

Defaults comparison is the one-line verdict: whether the assessment agreed with the package defaults. If it says it matched, there is nothing to do and you can drop the assessment from your script.

Probes are the measurements behind the recommendation. The optimizer table gives elapsed time and the log-likelihood each candidate reached in the probe budget, so a candidate that is fast but reaches a worse log-likelihood is not actually better. The solver table shows the three fastest direct factorizations split into setup and solve time; setup dominates when a fit re-factorizes often, solve time when the focal set is large. Notes collects anything that needs attention, such as a solver that failed to converge during probing.

See also

terradish_assess_settings for the assessment itself and what each component holds, terradish_solver_benchmark for benchmarking solvers alone, and terradish for the fit the recommendations feed. See vignette("v11-large-landscapes", package = "terradish") for when this is worth running.

Other solver settings: slim_terradish(), terradish_assess_settings(), terradish_solver_benchmark()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude), terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# coarsened for the example; assessment earns its keep on large graphs
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords[keep])

assessment <- terradish_assess_settings(
  Fst ~ forestcover + altitude,
  data = surface, measurement_model = mlpe, probe_maxit = 2)

assessment                      # the four-part report described above
#> terradish setting assessment
#> Graph: 2531 vertices, 9815 edges, 31 focal sites
#> Conductance parameters: 2 
#> 
#> Recommended settings:
#>   optimizer: newton (fastest acceptable probe: newton_hager_zhang)
#>   line search: HagerZhangControl
#>   solver: direct (fastest direct solver probe: simplicial_ldl + cholmod_cpp)
#>   solver_control:
#> $factorization
#> [1] "simplicial_ldl"
#> 
#> $solve_backend
#> [1] "cholmod_cpp"
#> 
#>   approximation: none (exact full-resolution fit)
#> 
#> Defaults comparison: Assessment differs from terradish defaults: solver_control tuned from terradish defaults.
#> 
#> Optimizer probes:
#>               label elapsed loglik gradient_evaluations hessian_evaluations
#>  newton_hager_zhang    0.19   1495                   10                   4
#>    bfgs_hager_zhang    0.14   1494                    8                   1
#>         bfgs_armijo    0.14   1492                    5                   1
#>  line_search_trials status
#>                   6     OK
#>                   5     OK
#>                   2     OK
#> 
#> Fastest direct solver probes:
#>   factorization solve_backend setup_time solve_time total_time
#>  simplicial_ldl   cholmod_cpp          0   0.000691          0
#>   simplicial_ll        matrix          0   0.000000          0
#>   supernodal_ll        matrix          0   0.000000          0
#> 
assessment$comparison$summary   # one-line verdict against the defaults
#> [1] "Assessment differs from terradish defaults: solver_control tuned from terradish defaults."
assessment$recommended$solver   # the settings, ready to reuse
#> [1] "direct"
# }
